speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual start. Let's be precise: when you say your gait is ataxic, do you feel like you are stumbling, or does it feel like your legs are moving in slow motion?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description sounds like significant cerebellar involvement. Is this ataxia constant, or does it worsen when you try to reach for something or touch your nose? Also, do you have any history of head trauma, autoimmune disorders, or recent infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for sharing that; natalizumab is a potent immunomodulator, and your Crohn's disease adds a layer of complexity to this. Has your vision ever blurred, or have you experienced double vision since starting this medication? Also, have you noticed any involuntary eye movements, like nystagmus?
